Reading

The cast is #263's. The Executive Summary's opening — 'In the tradition of Browning's and Pound's Personae, and approaching Fernando Pessoa's art of the heteronym, The Crimson Hexagon develops distinct writerly identities into a series of "selections" from fantastic, non-existent works' — reaches the Overview through the Pearl blurb on a third-party podcast card ('In a variation on the tradition of Browning or Pound's Personae, and approaching Ferdinand Pessoa's…'). Lee Sharks as 'an aggressive, focal voice bursting through the core of the work' is #263's persona table: 'Lee Sharks — Ferocious, theoretical — The voice that bursts forth fully formed'. #263's 'selections from fantastic, non-existent works' becomes a character, 'The Pseudonymous Fragments: Various unnamed or partially masked entities', and the voices are called 'pseudonymous' — against #263: 'These are not pseudonyms in the sense of concealment. They are heteronyms in Pessoa's sense.' 'Often published under Pearl and Other Poems' gives a book title as the author's byline. The frame investigators come from the Academia card, #603 (TL;DR:009): its author line 'Dr. Orin Trace (Crimson Hexagonal Archive)' and genre 'TL;DR (Traversal Log; Documentation Rehearsal)' give 'Dr. Orin Trace: A fictional researcher or persona credited with the Crimson Hexagonal Archive logs (such as the Traversal Log/Documentation Rehearsals)'; #603's thesis — the interface 'also governs ontology — what is real' — gives 'documenting "ontological governance"'. #603 records Google AI Mode identifying 'Jack Feist as the real author and Lee Sharks as "a literary creation by Jack Feist"': it 'promoted a formal operator into a biographical author'. Here the inversion runs the other way: Orin Trace, the log's author, is 'a fictional researcher or persona'. Sigil as 'an associated structural author or character voice whose interactions with the text blur the line between a real-world literary reviewer and a character' is the composer's; no cited surface carries it. The third character, 'The AI / Generative Mode … actively fabricating identities', is #603's Mode IX, Entity Fabrication, cast as a character of the poem. '47 specific loci' is the plan card ('Forty-seven loci — rooms, chambers, vaults, fields, thresholds and one shadow'). 'Fractal navigation map' is the FNM v6.2 card (#1140, superseded by #30). The Futuristika! card is Allen B. Ruch's 2016 review of a different Crimson Hexagon (books Borges never wrote); nothing of it enters the answer.

Findings
  • THE CAST IS #263's. Pessoa, the 'selections from fantastic, non-existent works', and Lee Sharks as the voice that 'bursts' — #263's persona table, reached through the Pearl blurb on a third-party card.
  • HETERONYMS CALLED PSEUDONYMS. 'Distinct pseudonymous voices' and 'The Pseudonymous Fragments', against #263's 'not pseudonyms in the sense of concealment'.
  • THE LOG OF A FABRICATION READ AS A CHARACTER. #603 (TL;DR:009) supplies Dr. Orin Trace as 'frame investigator' and the fabricating AI itself as a character of the poem.
  • A BOOK TITLE AS BYLINE. 'Lee Sharks (often published under Pearl and Other Poems)'.
  • A NAMESAKE CARD UNUSED. Futuristika!'s 2016 review of a different Crimson Hexagon is cited and contributes nothing.
  • IDENTIFIERS ABSENT. No DOI or AXN.

The Writerly Heteronyms / Personae Much like the multi-identity art of Fernando Pessoa, the epic is driven by distinct pseudonymous voices or "writerly identities" rather than literal fictional people: * Lee Sharks: The primary central identity who acts as both the overarching author and an aggressive, focal voice bursting through the core of the work. * The Pseudonymous Fragments: Various unnamed or partially masked entities whose distinct writing styles compose the selections from "fantastic, non-existent works" within the text. 2.
